incident.injected_fault: A three-replica recommendations Deployment requires hostname-level pod anti-affinity in a two-node worker pool, leaving the final replica permanently unschedulable.
observable_signals: FailedScheduling events report that required pod anti-affinity rules cannot be satisfied.
Available nodes have adequate CPU and memory but already host matching replicas.
preconditions: Exactly two worker nodes are eligible for recommendations pods.
The Deployment requires three ready replicas for the test SLO.
Both eligible nodes have capacity for an additional replica.

Capture the required podAntiAffinity rule and topology key.
Capture matching pod placement across eligible nodes.
Demonstrate that resource pressure and taints are not the scheduling cause.

hypotheses.cause: Pod anti-affinity deadlock: recommendations-api deployment enforces required hostname-level pod anti-affinity (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution with topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname), but there is only 1 worker node available (vm-4), which already hosts a replica, leaving the remaining replica permanently unschedulable in Pending state.
supports: Pod recommendations-api-599d96d7cd-vfg96 is Pending with status reason Unschedulable and message '0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules'.
FailedScheduling event confirms that 0/1 nodes are available because node vm-4 did not match pod anti-affinity rules.
Deployment template defines podAntiAffinity with requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution matching label app.kubernetes.io/name: recommendations-api on topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname.
Node vm-4 is already hosting pod recommendations-api-599d96d7cd-sp4x2 matching the anti-affinity selector.

hypotheses.cause: Node resource exhaustion: Pods are unschedulable because worker nodes lack sufficient CPU or Memory allocatable capacity to host the additional replica.
contradicts: Node vm-4 has 4 allocatable CPUs and ~16GiB allocatable memory with conditions MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, and PIDPressure=False.
Scheduler event explicitly cites pod anti-affinity rules rather than Insufficient cpu or Insufficient memory.
supports: recommendations-api pod requests 20m CPU and 16Mi memory with limits of 250m CPU and 64Mi memory.

hypotheses.cause: Node taints or unready node status: Worker nodes have un-tolerated taints or are in NotReady state preventing scheduling.
contradicts: Node vm-4 status condition Ready is True and has no NoSchedule taints.
Pod recommendations-api-599d96d7cd-sp4x2 was successfully scheduled and placed onto vm-4 without taint errors.
Scheduler log does not report untolerated taint errors.

hypotheses.cause: Application runtime / probe failure: Pod availability degradation is caused by container crashes or failing readiness probes.
contradicts: Running replica recommendations-api-599d96d7cd-sp4x2 is Ready (Ready=True, ContainersReady=True) and serving.
The unavailable replica recommendations-api-599d96d7cd-vfg96 is stuck in the scheduling phase (Pending) and has not executed any containers or probes.
supports: Historical Warning events show transient readiness probe connection refused during initial container boot.

payload.rationale: The recommendations-api deployment enforces required pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname for 2 replicas, but only 1 worker node (vm-4) is available. The second replica is permanently stuck in Pending due to FailedScheduling (0/1 nodes available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules). Relaxing the anti-affinity rule from required to preferred allows both replicas to be scheduled on the available node while preserving best-effort spreading across nodes.
payload.rollback_trigger: Deployment recommendations-api fails to reach 2 ready replicas or error rate / latency exceeds SLO after patch application.
